mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous three months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of periods with sustained HOUST increase, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with subsequent earnings reductions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals an aggressive tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL does not correlate with tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with improved consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous three months signals increased consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of periods with sustained RSAFS increase, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% over the previous two months and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a strong supply-side expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% and GDPC1 increase > 2% QoQ
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of INDPRO and GDPC1 increases does not correlate with increased corporate earnings.
